eligibility_rationale: Multiple floral traits have pollinator- and herbivore-linked selection across eight populations; trait-specific axes must be separated before ecological sign coding.
Herbivory is the upstream treatment and changes floral display/pollinator behavior; antagonist response to the same floral coordinate is not measured.
Pollination and herbivory are factorially manipulated and mediate selection on multiple floral traits on one female-fitness scale; each trait requires its own axis.
One declared fragrance contrast is manipulated and linked to pollinator response, florivore response and seed-production direction in the same experiment.
Landscape and herbivory alter display, pollination and seed set, but antagonist response to the same floral coordinate is not a paired function of A.
Genetic linkage among floral and herbivory-induced volatiles is measured without focal pollinator and antagonist response functions on one trait axis.
A common upstream soil amendment changes growth, flowers, visitors, herbivore performance and yield; the floral coordinate is not isolated as the shared causal axis.
Morph-specific floral and nectar traits, pollinators, robbers and seed production are reported, but the current audit does not yet establish which individual trait coordinates carry both functions.
The same synthetic floral scent coordinate elicits adult feeding and oviposition responses, but there is no common plant reproductive outcome linking the two functions.
Aphid infestation changes floral cues and pollinator behavior, but antagonist response to the altered floral coordinate is not measured.
One flower-colour axis is linked to pollinator- and seed-predator-mediated paths on reproductive output within one population.
Morph/organ-position differences are linked to legitimate visitation, nectar-robbing behavior and fruit/seed output across six populations and two years.
Nectar is experimentally manipulated for oviposition, but the focal experiment lacks a same-study pollinator response to the nectar coordinate.
The same sesquiterpenoid axis tracks both visitor roles across taxa, but no common reproductive outcome links the two routes.
The inflorescence display is tested for herbivore response while pollinator attraction comes from prior work rather than the same study.
The beta-ocimene axis is linked to bees and crab spiders across multiple populations and contexts, but the present audit does not yet provide one common-A reproductive decomposition for H1.
Colour and scent predict seed-predator host choice, but the same study does not measure the matching pollination response on those axes.
Benzylacetone is manipulated and both pollinator and antagonist routes are measured across complementary assays, but the outcomes are split rather than one common reproductive scale.
A genetically based scape-height morph is linked to pollinator- and grazer-mediated selection and mature-fruit fitness across replicated populations/experiments.
Component-specific scent manipulations identify florivore functions, but matching same-component pollinator responses are not measured in the focal experiment.
One showy-bract area axis is linked to pollinator and seed-predator selection on an observational reproductive-fitness decomposition.
One flower-colour axis is linked to pollinator visitation/community, seed-predation escape and plant-fitness selection across 12 populations.
